subject: Order Form redlines: indemnity and fine-tuning carveouts
messages:
From: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@medisure.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com, contracts@medisure.com
Cc: tim.holloway@medisure.com
Date: 2028-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MediSure - Order Form redlines (indemnity)

Hi Avery / Redwood team,

Thanks for the updated Order Form. We've run it by Legal and have a few outstanding indemnity concerns before procurement can sign. High level: MediSure needs (1) a firm indemnity for third-party IP claims that arise from using the Service (including claims related to model outputs that allegedly infringe third-party IP), (2) an express carve-in for customer-side fine-tuning if Redwood provides weights or tooling, and (3) no cap for third-party IP claims related to customer products built on your API.

I've attached our redlines (MS-OrderForm-v2-redlines.pdf) and marked the clauses we consider dealbreakers. Can we get a response to the attached redline spreadsheet and a redline-friendly summary of Redwood's defending-and-indemnifying positions by EOD next Wednesday? Procurement is aiming to finish contracting by 2028-02-22.

Thanks,
Sandra Lopez
Legal Counsel | MediSure Inc.

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-02-15T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: FW: MediSure - Order Form redlines (indemnity)

Looping you all in. MediSure pushed back hard on our indemnity carveouts and want outputs included + no cap on IP claims for customer products. They flagged fine-tuning as a carve-in if we supply weights/tooling. Procurement target is 2/22.

My read: we should avoid unlimited exposure for outputs and limit indemnity to Redwood-controlled code/weights. Kimberly/Neha, need negotiation position and acceptable fallback (cap/insurance ask). Ben, pls prep commercial note on why we can't accept output indemnity as-is.

Avery
Account Exec
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-02-16T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: MediSure - Order Form redlines (indemnity)

Avery / Ben — 

Thanks for the ping. Summary of legal posture and suggested compromise below.

What MediSure is asking:
- Indemnity for third-party IP claims caused by model outputs (broad)
- Indemnity for customer fine-tuning-related claims if Redwood provides weights/tooling
- No cap for claims tied to customer products

Risks for Redwood: open-ended exposure from customer-productization of outputs, attribution difficulty (hard to prove whether an output or customer prompt caused infringement), and moral hazard if customers expect us to cover downstream integration risks.

Recommended position (negotiation playbook):
1) Accept indemnity for third-party IP claims only where the claim is directly caused by Redwood-owned model artifacts we distribute (e.g., proprietary model weights or Redwood-published code) or by Redwood modifications to open models under our control.
2) Exclude indemnity for outputs generally and any customer fine-tuning unless Redwood materially supplied and managed weight distribution as a discrete service (i.e., we operate the fine-tune job and host the resulting weights under Redwood-managed infra). If we do accept a carve-in, require recordkeeping (logs, training data provenance) and elevate to a higher pricing tier.
3) Propose a cap on liability tied to the order value or a fixed aggregate cap — suggested cap: USD 5,000,000 for this enterprise order (negotiable).
4) Include standard notice and right-to-defend clauses (we want control of defense and settlement approval to avoid bad settlements).
5) Require certificate of insurance (commercial liability + technology E&O) with minimum limits to backstop.

If Sales wants to trade on price, we can offer a limited expansion of coverage as a premium add-on (insurance-first solution) rather than unlimited indemnity.

I'll draft a redline response and a short FAQ for Sales.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-02-16T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: MediSure - Order Form redlines (indemnity)

Agree with Kimberly. Two commercial notes to add when we go back:
- Highlight that our hosted models are maintained and improved over time; we can't warrant absence of third-party IP in downstream outputs because training data provenance is varied (we can offer model provenance docs but not absolute indemnity).
- Offer a pragmatic workaround: a limited indemnity for Redwood-distributed artifacts + a SOC2/forensic evidence playbook that we will follow during any claim, plus a POI (proof-of-origin) request process. That lets them feel concreteness without us taking unlimited risk.

I'll draft a short customer-facing summary.
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: sandra.lopez@medisure.com, tim.holloway@medisure.com, contracts@medisure.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-02-17T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MediSure - Order Form redlines (indemnity)

Sandra / Tim —

Appreciate the clear redlines and timing. We reviewed internally and want to propose a compromise to move toward your 2/22 procurement deadline:

Proposal (compromise wording, summary):
1) Redwood will defend and indemnify MediSure for third-party IP claims to the extent the claim arises from: (a) Redwoods proprietary model code or model weights that Redwood has expressly distributed to MediSure; or (b) a material bug or infringement introduced by Redwood in our hosted runtime.
2) Redwood will NOT provide indemnity for claims based solely on model outputs or for downstream products built by MediSure that incorporate Service outputs, except where Redwood has separately agreed in writing to accept such risk (premium add-on).
3) If MediSure requests fine-tuning services where Redwood hosts and manages the training job and stores resulting weights, we can discuss a separate addendum that includes a bespoke indemnity and enhanced logging/provenance requirements.
4) Aggregate liability cap for covered IP indemnity: USD 5,000,000 for the Order Form (we are open to discussing a higher cap with proportional pricing or insurance proof).
5) Commercial prerequisites: timely notice of claims, Redwoods right to control defense and settlement, and proof of MediSures compliance with acceptable-use restrictions and prompt-level best practices.
6) Redwood will provide SOC2 summary and can supply an evidence playbook to support triage; we've attached SOC2-summary.pdf and the redline response as a clean redline.

If that sounds workable, Kimberly will send formal redlines to your counsel and we can loop procurement to confirm payment/insurance mechanics. Happy to hop on a short call this week to close.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
Attachments: MS-OrderForm-Redwood-response.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

Avery / Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick response and the clear compromise language. A few follow-ups from Legal: 

1) MediSure can live with the carve-out on outputs as long as Redwood agrees to an expanded definition: if Redwood provides a "managed fine-tuning" service (you host the training job and deliver hosted weights that we use in production), MediSure wants that included in the indemnity (not as a separate paid add-on). We view managed fine-tuning as core to the product we are buying and don't want to buy a separate policy.

2) MediSure requests that the defense-control clause be mutual for settlements exceeding USD 250,000 (i.e., Redwood still leads defense but major settlements require mutual consent).

3) On the cap: can you confirm $5M is maximum aggregate for IP indemnity under the Order Form? Procurement wants a written confirmation and a placeholder for bumping limits if we show certificate of insurance.

We can take your redline and return with small edits if you confirm the two bullets above. Procurement remains on the 2/22 timeline.

Best,
Sandra Lopez
Legal Counsel | MediSure Inc.
Attachments: none
